blocks.text: Kidneys filter metabolic wastes and extra water from the blood and excrete them as urine. Urine forms in three steps in the nephron: glomerular filtration, selective reabsorption and tubular secretion.

Glomerular filtration (ultrafiltration) is a physical process. The efferent arteriole is narrower than the afferent arteriole, so blood in the glomerular capillaries stays at a relatively high pressure. This pressure forces water, urea, glucose, amino acids, vitamins and salts (Na+, K+, Cl-) out of the blood into Bowman's capsule. About one fifth (20%) of the fluid part of the blood filters into the capsule as glomerular filtrate. Plasma proteins (albumin, globulins) and blood cells are too large to pass the capillary walls and stay in the blood.
The filtrate holds vital nutrients as well as wastes. Selective reabsorption moves useful materials from the renal tubule back into the peritubular capillaries.

items: Proximal convoluted tubule: most reabsorption happens here; about 75% of the water returns by osmosis, and glucose, amino acids and salts (sodium, potassium, calcium) return by active transport.
Descending limb of the loop of Henle: more water is reabsorbed.
Ascending limb: impermeable to water, but actively transports salts out of the tubule.
Distal convoluted tubule: some water and salts are absorbed.
Collecting duct: the final site of water reabsorption.

blocks.text: Tubular secretion is the opposite of reabsorption: epithelial cells of the distal convoluted tubule take materials from the surrounding blood and secrete them into the filtrate. These include hydrogen ions, ammonium, potassium ions and metabolic toxins or drug residues such as penicillin. By secreting hydrogen ions the kidneys help keep the acid-base balance (pH) of the blood.

From the collecting ducts urine flows through the renal pelvis into a ureter and on to the urinary bladder; contractions of the bladder force it out through the urethra. A normal adult passes 1 to 2 L of urine a day. The amount varies: more water or fluids raise urine output, a salty diet makes the body retain water and lowers it, and exercise lowers it because water is lost in breathing and sweat.

blocks.title: Excretion and osmoregulation
blocks.text: While excreting wastes the kidneys also osmoregulate: they make dilute urine when body fluids are hypotonic and concentrated urine when body fluids are hypertonic or the body is dehydrated. In hot weather more water is lost as sweat, so the kidneys conserve water and make a small volume of concentrated urine.
